mona: Dumping a design thought: "probabilistic lease stamps" + tenant-backpressure credits to reduce per-prefix state and avoid oscillation across eviction-slabs. short sketch and tradeoffs below.

diego: quick TL;DR?

mona: Keep a tiny 1-byte stamp per-prefix (0-255) encoding recency/confidence plus a 1-byte credit counter per-tenant used for backpressure. Eviction picks low-stamp prefixes but must pay credits; credits are earned by sustained quietness or explicit tenant throttling.

anya: How do we keep correctness for handoff/write auth?

mona: Full lease remains canonical. Stamps drive only speculative eviction/admit. On any handoff or write we validate against full lease. If validation fails we revert eviction and decrement tenant credits.

mona: sketch:
```
// 2 bytes per-prefix minimal
struct ProbStamp { u8_recency; u8_flags; }
// per-tenant credits: small saturating counter
fn select_eviction(candidate_prefixes) -> PrefixId
// eviction pays tenant credits; if insufficient, prefix deferred
```

diego: Edgecase: prefix re-create or tombstone reuse -> recency wrap. How detect?

mona: include a node-global epoch bit in flags rotated on major GC / compaction. If stamp epoch != node epoch we treat stamp as stale and force full-lease consult next time.

anya: Observability: stamp_conflicts (cases where eviction decision disagrees w/ full), credit_depletions, speculative_eviction_rate, rollback_latency. Also track per-tenant churn and p50/p99 revert counts.

diego: Rollout: feature-flag behind canary; initial mode = read-only metrics only. Gate to go-wide: speculative_eviction_rate < 0.05% and rollback_latency < 200ms for 24h. Need kill-switch to disable speculative evict and refund credits.

mona: operational notes: credits are tunable (earn-rate, burn-cost). Default: earn-rate 1 credit/min per quiet tenant, eviction cost 3 credits. Small tenants get lower cost. Add a daily audit job that samples K prefixes and compares spec vs full decisions.

pager-bot: incident-bot: if speculative_eviction_rate > 0.2% alert to #eng-oncall.

anya: I like this for memory reduction and backpressure behavior; main risk is subtle fairness bugs. RFC should include math for credit dynamics and worst-case revert bounds.

mona: I'll draft RFC with microbenchmarks and a simulation harness (stochastic churn sim). booking a sync Fri 9:30 to review. thanks :sparkles:
